chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have hired workers, so we make them cultivate. They come to us and say: We have estimated this crop to be such and such. So give it to us, and we guarantee for you that we will give you your share based on this estimate.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it has matured?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with this.' I said: 'Then after that he comes to us and says: The estimate did not turn out as I estimated, and it has decreased.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So when it increases, does he return [the excess] to you?' I said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So you may take it with the complete estimate. Just as when it increases it is for him, similarly when it decreases it is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on agricultural sharecropping contracts based on estimated yield?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of 'hazr' (estimation) in sharecropping, a practice where the tenant guarantees a specific yield based on an initial assessment. Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the risk of variance—whether the crop exceeds or falls short of the estimate—remains with the worker, ensuring fairness and preventing dispute over the final distribution. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for validating commercial flexibility in agriculture while maintaining contractual integrity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For us are hired workers, so we make them cultivate, so they are answering and are saying to us, ‘We have estimated this plantation with such and such. So give it to us and we would guarantee for you that we would give you your share upon this estimate’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A has it matured?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with this’. 
I said, ‘So he comes after that and he is saying to us, ‘The estimated did not come out to be as we had estimated it to be, and it is deficient’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So when it is more, does he return to you?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So for you is that you take it with the complete estimated just as when it is more it would be for him, similar to that, when it is deficient it is upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from certain persons of his people who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the people who work for hire and we make a deal with them to farm for us and they say, ‘We have estimated this farm for so and so much and if you give it to us we guarantee your share according to our estimation.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is it completed?’ I replied, ‘Yes, it is complete.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’ I then asked, ‘He afterward comes and says that estimation is not as it was supposed to be and it is less.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do they return to you if it is more than estimated?’ I replied, ‘No, they do not return to us anything.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You have the right to take according to the estimation, just as when it is more than estimation, they keep the extra, so also it is on them if it is less than estimation.’”
